[Page 1] HOMESHIELD INSURANCE GROUP Synthetic Data – Training Use Only Page 1 | HomeShield Insurance Group | Policy Year 2025 HOME INSURANCE GLOSSARY OF TERMS HomeShield Insurance Group | Reference Document | 2025 Accidental Damage Sudden and unexpected damage that is the result of an unintentional action, such as spilling wine on a carpet or breaking a window. Not the same as wear and tear, mechanical breakdown, or damage caused by neglect. Buildings Sum Insured The amount your buildings are insured for, which should represent the full cost to rebuild the property from scratch (rebuild cost), including site clearance, professional fees, and VAT. This is NOT the same as the market value of the property. Contents Sum Insured The total replacement value of all your household contents at current new prices. Should be calculated on a new-for-old basis. Escape of Water Damage caused by water

ement value of all your household contents at current new prices. Should be calculated on a new-for-old basis. Escape of Water Damage caused by water leaking or escaping from internal pipes, tanks, plumbing systems, or fixed appliances. One of the most frequent home insurance claims in the UK. Excess The first portion of any claim that you pay yourself before the insurer pays the remainder. Different types of excess may apply: standard excess, voluntary excess (chosen by you for a premium reduction), and compulsory excess (e.g., subsidence excess of £1,000). Flood The overflow of a body of water (river, lake, sea, reservoir) or the accumulation of rainwater on land that is normally dry, causing damage to the insured property. Groundwater seepage and drain surcharge are not classified as flood. Flood Re A UK government-backed reinsurance scheme that allows insurers to offer affordable flo

epage and drain surcharge are not classified as flood. Flood Re A UK government-backed reinsurance scheme that allows insurers to offer affordable flood cover to homes in high-risk flood zones. Properties built before 1 January 2009 in eligible flood risk areas can be placed in the Flood Re scheme. Heave The upward or sideways movement of the ground beneath the buildings, typically caused by the expansion of clay soils when moisture content increases (e.g., following the removal of a large tree). High-Value Items Limit The maximum total amount HomeShield will pay for all specially listed (scheduled) high-value items in a single claim. Items must be individually listed on the policy. Indemnity Basis A claims settlement basis where the insurer pays the current market value of the item at the time of loss, taking depreciation into account. The opposite of new-for-old. HomeShield uses new-fo

r pays the current market value of the item at the time of loss, taking depreciation into account. The opposite of new-for-old. HomeShield uses new-for-old for contents under 8 years old. Landlord's Contents Furniture, furnishings, and appliances provided by the landlord to tenants as part of a furnished tenancy. Covered under the Landlord Plus plan up to the contents sum insured. Legal Expenses Cover An optional (or included) add-on that pays for legal fees to pursue or defend disputes relating to your home, such as property damage disputes, contractor disputes, and (for Landlord Plus) tenancy disputes. Loss Adjuster An independent professional appointed by the insurer to investigate, assess, and report on a claim. Loss adjusters are typically appointed for large, complex, or contested claims. Damage caused by tenants is covered under Landlord Plus only. New-for-Old A claims settlement basis where the insurer replaces damaged or stolen items with equivalent new items, without applying depreciation. HomeShield applies new-for-old to contents items less than 8 years old. Outbuilding A detached structure within the boundary of the insured property that is not the main dwelling, such as a garage, garden shed, summer house, or workshop. Covered for buildings damage up to £15,000; contents in outbuildings covered up to £2,500. Peril A specific risk or cause of loss that is covered by an insurance poli

dings damage up to £15,000; contents in outbuildings covered up to £2,500. Peril A specific risk or cause of loss that is covered by an insurance policy (e.g., fire, flood, theft, storm). Standard home insurance covers named perils only. Property Owners' Liability Liability cover for bodily injury or property damage suffered by third parties (including tenants) as a result of a defect in the insured property. Included in all HomeShield plans. Rebuild Cost The cost to completely rebuild your property from scratch if it were totally destroyed, including demolition, site clearance, materials, labour, and professional fees. This is the correct basis for your buildings sum insured. It is NOT the market value of your property. Scheduled Item A high-value item that is individually listed on the policy with a description and agreed value, so that it is covered for its full replacement value rath

gh-value item that is individually listed on the policy with a description and agreed value, so that it is covered for its full replacement value rather than just the single article limit. Single Article Limit The maximum amount HomeShield will pay for any one item or matched set, unless the item is scheduled (listed) on the policy. Standard: £1,500; Comprehensive: £3,000. Storm An event characterised by winds exceeding Beaufort Scale Force 10 (approximately 55 mph), or exceptional and sustained rainfall, hail, or snow that causes physical damage to the insured property. Normal rainfall, even if heavy, does not constitute a storm. Subsidence The downward movement of the ground beneath the foundations of the insured buildings, causing structural damage. Subject to a £1,000 compulsory excess. Excluded for properties under 10 years old (normal settlement) and for coastal/river erosion. Trac

ural damage. Subject to a £1,000 compulsory excess. Excluded for properties under 10 years old (normal settlement) and for coastal/river erosion. Trace and Access The cost of locating and gaining access to the source of a water or oil leak, including cutting through walls, floors, or ceilings and making good afterwards. Covered up to £5,000 under all HomeShield plans. Underinsurance The situation where the sum insured is less than the true value of the insured property or contents. If underinsurance is identified at the time of a claim, HomeShield may reduce the claim payment proportionately (averaging). Voluntary Excess An amount you agree to pay on top of the compulsory excess in exchange for a reduction in your premium. If you choose a voluntary excess of £250 and the compulsory excess is £150, you will pay the first £400 of any claim. DISCLAIMER: Synthetic data for training use only.

Project Overview Group 04 is tasked with building a production-grade Property & Home Insurance AI Copilot — an intelligent assistant that supports homeowners and claims handlers through the full prope

a production-grade Property & Home Insurance AI Copilot — an intelligent assistant that supports homeowners and claims handlers through the full property insurance lifecycle: policy coverage Q&A, damage assessment guidance, repair cost estimation, claim filing assistance, contractor network lookup, and claim status tracking. The key technical differentiator for this project is Agentic RAG with Persistent Conversational Memory. Unlike a stateless Q&A bot, this system remembers what the user has shared across turns — property details, damage descriptions, claim IDs, and coverage type — and uses that accumulated context to provide progressively richer, more personalised responses without asking the user to repeat themselves. A multi-tool dispatch layer routes queries to the appropriate specialised tool based on intent. Domain Property & Home Insurance AI Pattern Agentic RAG + Persistent Mem

Problem Statement When a home is damaged — by fire, flood, storm, theft, or structural failure — the policyholder enters a stressful, document-heavy claims process. They must understand what their policy covers, document the damage correctly, get repair estimates, find approved contractors, file the claim accurately, and track it

tand what their policy covers, document the damage correctly, get repair estimates, find approved contractors, file the claim accurately, and track its progress. Each of these steps currently requires separate interactions with different systems and agents. The compounding problem is memory loss across interactions. A homeowner who called yesterday to describe storm damage to their roof should not have to repeat those details when they call back to ask about approved contractors. Claims handlers who gathered damage information in one session should be able to reference it in the next. The current stateless, siloed experience adds friction at exactly the moment the customer needs speed and clarity. ■ Your Mission Build a memory-augmented AI copilot that accumulates property context, damage descriptions, and claim details across conversation turns, and uses that persistent memory to answer

[Page 1] HOMESHIELD INSURANCE GROUP Synthetic Data – Training Use Only Page 1 | HomeShield Insurance Group | Policy Year 2025 CONTENTS & VALUABLES COVERAGE GUIDE HomeShield Insurance Group | 2025 Edition | Standard & Comprehensive Plans UNDERSTANDING YOUR CONTENTS SUM INSURED Calculating the Right Sum Insured Your contents sum insured must reflect the total cost to replace ALL your household belongings and personal possessions at current new prices (new-for-old basis). It is one of the most commonly underestimated figures in home insurance. HOW TO CALCULATE: Go room by room. For each room, list every item and its current replacement cost (not what you paid; not current second-hand value — what it would cost to buy new today). COMMON ROOMS AND ITEMS TO INCLUDE: Living Room: Sofas, chairs, TV, media equipment, carpets, curtains, ornaments, books, lamps. Bedroom: Beds, mattresses, wardrobes

ND ITEMS TO INCLUDE: Living Room: Sofas, chairs, TV, media equipment, carpets, curtains, ornaments, books, lamps. Bedroom: Beds, mattresses, wardrobes, clothing (total replacement value), bedding, jewellery, watches, handbags. Kitchen: White goods (fridge, washing machine, dishwasher), cookware, small appliances, crockery, cutlery. Home Office: Computer, printer, office furniture, work equipment. Garage / Outbuildings: Tools, lawn mower, bicycles, sports equipment. COMMON MISTAKE: Many policyholders forget to include: clothing (often worth £3,000–£8,000 for a typical family), children's toys and equipment, food and drink, garden furniture and equipment, and recently purchased high-value items. SINGLE ARTICLE LIMITS AND SCHEDULED ITEMS Single Article Limit Explained The single article limit is the MAXIMUM HomeShield will pay for any single item or pair/set of items, unless that item is sp

e Article Limit Explained The single article limit is the MAXIMUM HomeShield will pay for any single item or pair/set of items, unless that item is specifically listed (scheduled) on your policy. Standard Cover: £1,500 per item Comprehensive Cover: £3,000 per item EXAMPLE: You have a diamond ring worth £8,000. Your policy has a £3,000 single article limit. If it is not scheduled, HomeShield will pay only £3,000 for its loss — not £8,000. To be covered for the full £8,000, it must be specifically listed with a professional valuation. PAIRS AND SETS: If one item from a pair or matching set (e.g., a pair of earrings) is lost, HomeShield will not pay for the full set — only the proportionate value of the lost item. Consider this when scheduling matching sets. How to Schedule High-Value Items Step 1: Identify all items where the replacement value exceeds the single article limit. Step 2: Obta

matching sets. How to Schedule High-Value Items Step 1: Identify all items where the replacement value exceeds the single article limit. Step 2: Obtain a professional valuation: For jewellery and watches > £3,000: a valuation from a RICS-registered jewellery valuer, dated within 3 years. For artworks and antiques: a valuation from an authorised dealer or auction house, dated within 5 years. For collectibles: specialist appraisal from an accredited appraiser.
